display.purpose: Page-level headings on documentation surfaces. No component uses it.

headline.purpose: Dialog and Sheet titles only — the one place a component raises its voice.

title.purpose: Card titles and in-component section headings. Same size as body; weight does the work.

body.purpose: The interface voice: labels, menu rows, table cells and headers (headers at weight 600), input and button text. Most type in the system.

label.purpose: Badges, the small button size, tooltips, and the secondary labels inside menus and select panels.

mono.purpose: Code badges and inline code only.

themes.name: solace
themes.description: White canvas, graphite ink — muted signals, a reserved blue for action. The default.

themes.name: porcelain
themes.description: Cool porcelain ground with a cobalt accent, after blue-and-white ware.

themes.name: tobacco
themes.description: Warm paper and tobacco-brown ink with a taupe accent.

themes.name: marigold
themes.description: Warm cream with the system's one remaining violet accent, drawn at 3px.

themes.name: eucalyptus
themes.description: Cool green-grey paper with a teal-blue accent.

shadows.name: offset
shadows.purpose: Surface shade. Raised surfaces (cards). Static, never on a pressable.

shadows.name: offset-overlay
shadows.purpose: Overlay shade. Dialogs, sheets, menus, select panels — a darker grey for a higher layer. Static.

shadows.name: offset-action
shadows.purpose: Action edge. Revealed on hover under an edged pressable; held statically by an engaged writing field.

shadows.name: offset-action-hover
shadows.purpose: Grown action edge. Held by a trigger for as long as it owns an open overlay — open mirrors hover, one step louder.

shadows.name: offset-action-danger
shadows.purpose: Danger edge. Replaces the action edge on an invalid field under focus.

shadows.name: menu-leading-rule
shadows.purpose: The inset accent rule on the currently navigated menu or select row. 2px, because it marks engagement rather than mere proximity.

motion.name: duration-standard
motion.purpose: Every state transition: box-shadow, translate, border-color, background-color. The whole motion vocabulary for controls.

motion.name: duration-slow
motion.purpose: The single slower transition in the system: the determinate Progress indicator's scaleX. Nothing else uses it.

motion.name: navigation-progress
motion.purpose: The only looping animation: a bar sweeping across the navigation progress track. Overlays have no entrance animation at all.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce collapses every animation and transition globally in foundation.css.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Ink fill is the complete persistent emphasis signal; accent appears only on hover, open ownership, or keyboard focus.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 36px; padding: 0 16px; border-radius: 0; border: 1px solid transparent; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: box-shadow 100ms, translate 100ms, border-color 100ms, background-color 100ms; } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-border-focus, #2b5bff); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--color-bg-emphasis, #090909); color: var(--color-fg-on-emphasis, #fcfcfa); border-color: var(--color-border-strong, #090909); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, #2b5bff 24%, #090909); box-shadow: var(--shadow-offset-action, 1px 1px 0 0 #2b5bff); } .ds-btn-primary:active { background: color-mix(in oklab, #2b5bff 14%, #090909); box-shadow: none; translate: 1px 1px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Raised paper with a hairline border. Same edge grammar as primary, quieter material.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: var(--color-bg-raised, #f9f9f9); color: var(--color-fg, #090909); border-color: var(--color-border, #8c8c8c); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: var(--color-bg-hover, #ededed); box-shadow: var(--shadow-offset-action, 1px 1px 0 0 #2b5bff); } .ds-btn-secondary:active { background: var(--color-bg-active, #cbcbcb); box-shadow: none; translate: 1px 1px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Not an edged pressable. Its only hover signal is the grey fill — no accent edge, no press translation.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: var(--color-fg, #090909); border-color: transparent; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: var(--color-bg-hover, #ededed); } .ds-btn-ghost:active { background: var(--color-bg-active, #cbcbcb); }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Quiet at rest, cap-off on focus: a static accent edge and no outline. The caret carries the vivid voice.
components.html: <input class='ds-input' type='text' placeholder='Search components' aria-label='Search components' />
components.css: .ds-input { height: 36px; width: 100%; padding: 0 12px; border-radius: 0; border: 1px solid var(--color-border, #8c8c8c); background: var(--color-bg-input, #fcfcfa); color: var(--color-fg, #090909); font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 0.8125rem; caret-color: var(--color-accent-solid, #2b5bff); transition: box-shadow 100ms; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--color-fg-subtle, #666666); } .ds-input::selection { background: color-mix(in oklab, #2b5bff 17%, #fcfcfa); } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; box-shadow: var(--shadow-offset-action, 1px 1px 0 0 #2b5bff); } .ds-input[aria-invalid='true'] { border-color: var(--color-danger-solid, #a13d52); } .ds-input[aria-invalid='true']:focus { box-shadow: var(--shadow-offset-action-danger, 1px 1px 0 0 #a13d52); }

components.name: Card
components.description: A material, not a template: square corners, one hairline border, a drawn grey offset shade. Imposes no header/body/footer.
components.html:
Offset, not blur

Elevation is the trace a raised object leaves on paper.
components.css: .ds-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 16px; padding: 20px; border-radius: 0; border: 1px solid var(--color-border, #8c8c8c); background: var(--color-bg-raised, #f9f9f9); color: var(--color-fg, #090909); box-shadow: var(--shadow-offset, 1px 1px 0 0 #c4c4c4); font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; } .ds-card-title { margin: 0; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1; } .ds-card-desc { margin: 0; font-size: 0.8125rem; line-height: 1.4; color: var(--color-fg-muted, #535353); }

components.name: Checkbox
components.description: An instrument on a 24px chassis. Checked is ink plus a glyph, never accent; the chassis holds still while the glyph travels 1px under the press.
components.css: .ds-checkbox { position: relative; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 24px; height: 24px; border-radius: 0; border: 1px solid var(--color-border, #8c8c8c); background: var(--color-bg-emphasis, #090909); color: var(--color-fg-on-emphasis, #fcfcfa); cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 100ms, box-shadow 100ms; } .ds-checkbox::before { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: -11px; } .ds-checkbox:hover { box-shadow: var(--shadow-offset-action, 1px 1px 0 0 #2b5bff); } .ds-checkbox:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-border-focus, #2b5bff); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-checkbox-glyph { transition: transform 100ms; } .ds-checkbox:active .ds-checkbox-glyph { transform: translate(1px, 1px); }

components.name: Switch
components.description: A track, not a square choice. Ink fills the track when checked; the thumb travels while the chassis stays fixed.
components.css: .ds-switch { position: relative; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; width: 36px; height: 20px; padding: 2px; border-radius: 0; border: 1px solid var(--color-border, #8c8c8c); background: var(--color-bg-emphasis, #090909); cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 100ms, box-shadow 100ms; } .ds-switch::before { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: -15px; } .ds-switch:hover { box-shadow: var(--shadow-offset-action, 1px 1px 0 0 #2b5bff); } .ds-switch:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-border-focus, #2b5bff); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-switch-thumb { display: block; width: 12px; height: 12px; background: var(--color-bg-input, #fcfcfa); transform: translateX(18px); transition: transform 100ms; } .ds-switch:active .ds-switch-thumb { transform: translate(19px, 1px); }

components.name: Navigation Strip
components.description: Cells fuse on shared hairlines with no gaps. The current cell paints an inset lens plate with a two-tone rim — glass laid over the page, not a highlight on the text.
components.html:
• Components
  • Tokens
  • Themes
components.css: .ds-nav { display: inline-block; border: 1px solid var(--color-border-muted, #aaaaaa); font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; } .ds-nav-list { display: inline-flex; margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; } .ds-nav-list > li + li { border-left: 1px solid var(--color-border-muted, #aaaaaa); } .ds-nav-item { position: relative; isolation: isolate; display: flex; align-items: center; height: 32px; padding: 0 14px; font-size: 0.8125rem; text-decoration: none; color: var(--color-fg, #090909); } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: var(--color-bg-hover, #ededed); } .ds-nav-item:active { background: var(--color-bg-active, #cbcbcb); } .ds-nav-item:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-border-focus, #2b5bff); outline-offset: 2px; z-index: 2; } .ds-nav-item-current { cursor: default; } .ds-nav-item-current:hover { background: transparent; } .ds-nav-item-current::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 4px; z-index: -1; background: color-mix(in oklab, #2b5bff 8%, #fcfcfa); border: 1px solid; border-top-color: var(--color-border-muted, #aaaaaa); border-left-color: var(--color-border-muted, #aaaaaa); border-right-color: var(--color-border-strong, #090909); border-bottom-color: var(--color-border-strong, #090909); }

components.name: Menu Item
components.description: The row you would act on takes the accent wash plus a 2px inset leading rule, with the label left in ink.
components.css: .ds-menu { min-width: 10rem; padding: 4px; border-radius: 0; border: 1px solid var(--color-border-strong, #090909); background: var(--color-bg-overlay, #f5f5f5); box-shadow: var(--shadow-offset-overlay, 1px 1px 0 0 #a0a0a0); font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; } .ds-menu-item { padding: 6px 8px; font-size: 0.8125rem; color: var(--color-fg, #090909); cursor: pointer; } .ds-menu-item-highlighted, .ds-menu-item:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, #2b5bff 17%, #fcfcfa); box-shadow: inset 2px 0 0 0 var(--color-accent-solid, #2b5bff); } .ds-menu-item-danger { color: color-mix(in oklab, #a13d52 50%, #090909); } .ds-menu-item-danger:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, #a13d52 17%, #fcfcfa); box-shadow: inset 2px 0 0 0 var(--color-danger-solid, #a13d52); }

components.name: Badge
components.description: Square, bordered, 11px. Ink with paper knockout by default; role variants always ship their own knockout foreground.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 0; border: 1px solid var(--color-border-strong, #090909); background: var(--color-bg-emphasis, #090909); color: var(--color-fg-on-emphasis, #fcfcfa); font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 500; } .ds-badge-danger { background: var(--color-danger-solid, #a13d52); border-color: var(--color-danger-solid, #a13d52); color: var(--color-danger-fg-on-solid, #fcfcfa); } .ds-badge-outline { background: transparent; border-color: var(--color-border, #8c8c8c); color: var(--color-fg, #090909); }

narrative.northStar: Ink & Instrument — a printed page you can press
narrative.overview:
Everything on screen is drawn, not lit. The references are the print shop and the machine shop: a well-set page, ruled forms, keys that travel when pressed. Corners are square, color is flat, borders are pen strokes, and shadows are offset marks with zero blur — the trace a raised object leaves on paper, not the glow of a light source. Nothing here emits light, because nothing printed does.

The system runs on one pen and one vivid voice. The neutral ramp is a single ink used at full strength for text, strong borders, and solid fills, so a line and a fill always agree about what matters. Ink is never diluted, only rationed: at 1px a stroke is either the ink voice or the hairline voice, with nothing in between. Against that monochrome ground, exactly one chromatic voice — the accent — is reserved for what you can act on. Signals (danger, success, warning, info) carry meaning but never emphasis, so a screen full of status never becomes a screen full of shouting.

Depth is semantic before it is spatial. A grey offset shade means "this is a raised surface"; an accent edge means "this responds to you." Pressables are neutral at rest, reveal a thin accent edge on hover, and drop onto it under the press. Writing fields stay quiet until engaged and then cap off with a static edge that leaves when the pen lifts. Small controls are instruments: the chassis stays put while the inner key — a check, a thumb, a label — travels one pixel. Brutalism supplies the refusals (no gradients, no blur, no rounding, nothing that lies about structure) but not the aggression. The goal is precision, not rawness.

Confirmed visual rejections. This must not look like shadcn/ui (too soft, too rounded, too close to what everyone ships), Material Design (too corporate, too systematic), Stripe or Linear (lit rather than drawn — glow, gradients, blurred elevation; the precision is shared, the material is not), Bootstrap (no point of view), or a web-brutalism showcase (aggression as the point). What a person should feel using it is confidence and clarity, respect for the craft, and material distinction — made, not assembled from the same lit parts as everything else.
keyCharacteristics: Square by default — 0 radius everywhere except Radio's circle.
One neutral ink at full strength; no mid-grey text, no diluted borders.
One chromatic accent, reserved for interaction — never for decoration.
Offset shadows with zero blur; grey for surfaces, accent for pressables.
Flat fills only. No gradient, no blur, no opacity used as a styling device.
Two-layer tokens: a theme writes 30 palette values, components read 68 semantic names and never touch a palette value directly.

rules.name: The One Pen Rule
rules.body: The neutral ramp is a single ink. Text, strong borders, and solid fills all come from the deepest step, so a line and a fill never disagree about importance. Ink is rationed, not diluted: a 1px stroke is either the ink voice (border-strong) or the hairline voice (border / border-muted). A "slightly softer black" does not exist at hairline width — measured, not asserted.

rules.name: The One Vivid Voice Rule
rules.body: The accent belongs solely to what you can act on. Hue carries meaning, never emphasis. If a mark is not focus, open ownership, hover intent, current selection, or a link, it does not get the accent.

rules.name: The Knockout Rule
rules.body: Every solid ships with its own foreground (danger-solid + danger-fg-on-solid). Never hand-pick a text color on a solid, and never mix roles — warning text on an info tint is a defect, not a variation.

rules.name: The Palette-Swap Rule
rules.body: Components consume only the 68 semantic names. A theme authors 30 palette values (--surface-0…2, --tone-0…11, --signal-*, --signal-*-on, --shadow-*) and nothing else. Writing --tone-4 or a raw hex inside a component is the one unforgivable color error: it breaks every theme at once. Dark mode is the same mechanism — a palette swap under prefers-color-scheme: dark, not a separate set of component rules.

rules.name: The Two-Size Rule
rules.body: 13px carries the interface and 11px carries labels. Together they are nearly every piece of type in the component set. Reaching past them is a claim that this element outranks the whole interface — Dialog and Sheet titles are the only components that earn it.

rules.name: The Weight-Before-Size Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy inside a component is made with weight (400 → 500 → 600) and with ink color (fg → fg-muted), not by growing the type. A card title is the same size as its body text.

rules.name: The Fused Strip Rule
rules.body: Navigation and tab cells do not float as separate chips. They share hairlines: each cell pulls back one pixel (-ml-px) so adjacent borders collapse into a single ruled seam, and the strip carries no standing edge of its own. Gaps between cells break the instrument.

rules.name: The 44px Rule
rules.body: Any control smaller than 44px carries an invisible hit expander (before:absolute before:inset-[-Npx] before:content-['']). Because the pseudo-element starts inside the border, both 1px borders count toward the measurement, and the inset varies by chassis: -11px on the 24px checkbox/radio, -15px on the switch, -14px on a 16px glyph button. Verify the real box in the browser, never by arithmetic on the class name alone.

rules.name: The Drawn-Not-Lit Rule
rules.body: Every shadow is <offset> <offset> 0 0 <color>. Blur radius and spread are always zero. A blurred shadow claims a light source, and nothing on a printed page emits light.

rules.name: The Shadow-Is-Voice Rule
rules.body: Grey shade = raised surface. Accent edge = pressable. A surface never takes the accent edge, and a pressable is never given a standing grey shade at rest.

rules.name: The Press-Drops-On Rule
rules.body: Pressing removes the shadow and translates the element one pixel toward it (active:shadow-none active:translate-x-px active:translate-y-px), so the control physically lands on the edge it revealed. Ghost and Link buttons opt out of both, because they never had an edge to drop onto.

rules.name: The Square Rule
rules.body: Radius is 0. The only circle in the system is Radio's chassis and its dot. If a new component wants a rounded corner, the answer is no — find the meaning that corner was carrying and draw it with a stroke.

rules.name: The Dashed-Disabled Rule
rules.body: Disabled always means the same four things: dashed border, border-muted stroke, bg-disabled fill, fg-disabled text — plus removal of every shadow and interaction affordance. Never opacity.

rules.name: The Focus-Outermost Rule
rules.body: Keyboard focus always owns the outermost mark: a 2px accent outline offset 2px on pressables, the cap-off edge on writing fields. Open ownership, hover, and current-selection cues all stay inside it, so a focused control is unmistakable even in a row of selected and open ones. When a field is invalid, danger replaces the accent in that indicator rather than layering over it.

rules.name: The One-Channel Rule
rules.body: Two cues never compete in the same visual channel. Open replaces the hover edge. Press drops the edge. Selection never borrows the focus outline. Disabled removes interaction edges and focus treatment entirely. Only spatially distinct channels may stack — most importantly, an outer focus outline around an open-owner edge or a selected fill.

rules.name: The Chassis Rule
rules.body: On an instrument, the chassis never moves. Only the inner key — a check, a dot, a thumb, a label — travels the 1px under a press.

dos: Do use only the 68 semantic token names (bg-bg-raised, text-fg-muted, border-border-strong). They are the entire color API.
Do pair every role solid with its own knockout (bg-danger-solid text-danger-fg-on-solid), and every role tint with its full triple (bg-{role}-bg + border-{role}-border + text-{role}-fg).

Do give pressables the neutral rest / accent-edge-on-hover / grown-edge-while-open / drop-on-press sequence (hover:shadow-offset-action data-[state=open]:shadow-offset-action-hover active:shadow-none active:translate-x-px active:translate-y-px).

Do use one focus grammar on pressables — focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-border-focus focus-visible:outline-offset-2 — and cap-off on writing fields: focus:outline-hidden not-read-only:focus:shadow-offset-action.
Do use the one disabled pattern everywhere: disabled:border-dashed disabled:border-border-muted disabled:bg-bg-disabled disabled:text-fg-disabled disabled:shadow-none.

Do add a hit expander — before:absolute before:inset-[-Npx] before:content-[''] — to any control under 44px, sized so the measured box clears 44: -11px on the 24px checkbox/radio chassis, -15px on the switch, -14px on a 16px glyph button. Verify it in a browser, not by arithmetic on the class name.
Do assign a variant's edge explicitly. shadow-none does not opt a variant out of a custom shadow-offset-action — tailwind-merge cannot dedupe a custom shadow utility against it.
donts: Don't write a palette value (--tone-4, --surface-1, --signal-accent) or a raw color inside a component. Palette values belong to themes only.
Don't add a border radius. rounded-lg, rounded-md, and rounded-sm have no place here; Radio's rounded-full is the sole exception.
Don't use a blurred shadow (shadow-md, shadow-lg, any non-zero blur or spread), a gradient, or a backdrop blur.
Don't use opacity as a styling device — not for disabled, not for muted text, not for hover. The modal scrim is the only alpha in the system.
Don't put a standing accent edge on an idle pressable, or any accent edge on a surface. Accent is a state, not a synonym for "interactive."
Don't let selection borrow the focus outline, or let hover and open cues stack in the same channel.
Don't give Ghost or Link buttons an edge or a press translation; they are not edged pressables.
Don't reach past 13px/11px for component type. Use weight and ink color for hierarchy instead.
Don't put gaps between navigation or tab cells — they fuse on shared hairlines.
